sources.entry: Kiwix - Kiwix for iOS and macOS, build on Swift.

summary.one_liner: Kiwix for Apple iOS and macOS, an offline reader for Web content (primarily Wikipedia) that reads ZIM archives, written in Swift.
summary.what_it_does: Kiwix is an offline reader for web content, mainly used to make Wikipedia available without a connection. It reads archives in the ZIM file format, a compressed open format with metadata. This repository holds the Apple version, supporting iOS and macOS. The README covers distribution through the App Store, Mac App Store, and a direct macOS download. It also documents the developer workflow: generating the Xcode project with XcodeGen, installing dependencies from a Brewfile including the CoreKiwix.xcframework (libkiwix and libzim), running unit and UI test schemes, and building the framework from source via kiwix-build. Deployment notes describe nightly builds, TestFlight publishing, and release steps.
use_cases: read Wikipedia offline on iPhone or iPad
read Wikipedia offline on a Mac
contribute to or build the Kiwix iOS/macOS app
how_to_run: Install Xcode, its command-line tools (xcode-select --install), and Homebrew
From the project folder run: brew bundle
Open the generated project in Xcode, set your Bundle Identifier and signing profile, then build and run
notable: Offline reading of ZIM archives, including Wikipedia
Single codebase for iOS and macOS
Xcode project generated from project.yml with XcodeGen, so project files are not tracked in git
Nightly signed and notarized macOS builds plus TestFlight publishing
caveats: Video in ZIM files works properly only from Kiwix 3.4.0, iOS 17.0, or macOS 14.0; older combinations are not fully supported
Building the CoreKiwix.xcframework from source requires kiwix-build, ninja, meson, and an iOS SDK for iOS builds
Development builds require an Apple Developer account for signing
